description: The hand-verified expected result for the positive Dependency-Check fixture. Every value was derived by reading the fixture and the authored contracts in harness/lib/normalize/, never by running the adapter and recording what it printed. Where this file and harness/lib/normalize/adapters/dependency_check.py disagree, the disagreement is the finding: diagnose it rather than overwriting this file to match.
reference_case_for: the four-level package-coordinate precedence -- three of the four levels are reached by a different row of this one fixture, and the fourth is named with the reason no row reaches it
label-over-score severity with the entry that governed recorded -- including a record whose label band and CVSS band disagree, and a record with no label at all where a score is selected from several
rules: No user-specified rule governs this file. review_rules returns exactly one line, 'No user rules provided.', which is the complete document; AAP 0.7 and AAP 0.10.2 say the same. Enterprise best practice applies in their place, held to the AAP's own bar: hand-verify rather than record a run, reject rather than infer, and state an absence rather than omit it. This file exists because of AAP 0.6.1, AAP 0.6.2 and AAP 0.9.4, not because of a rule.

captured_verbatim: reportSchema, scanInfo (all four NVD dataSource timestamps) and projectInfo -- byte-identical to the raw artifact
the dependency envelopes at indices 0, 1, 2, 3 and 7 -- isVirtual, fileName, filePath, md5, sha1, sha256 and evidenceCollected, byte-identical to the raw artifact's entry for the same fileName
authored_rather_than_captured: every packages[] array, and every vulnerabilities[] array
the dependency entries at indices 4, 5 and 6 -- dev/package-lock.json (virtual), ui-test/package-lock.json and docs/Gemfile.lock
fixture.why_not_a_pure_excerpt: The raw artifact carries 32 dependencies with ZERO vulnerabilities and ZERO packages, so no excerpt of it can exercise a single field of this adapter's row builder. AAP 0.6.1 asks for an unmodified captured excerpt, and for a tool that reported nothing that is unsatisfiable in the positive direction: what is captured verbatim is captured verbatim and named above, and what had to be authored is named too, so a reader can tell which is which rather than trusting the file's label. The three lockfile dependencies are absent from the raw artifact for a recorded reason: the runner passes 18 absolute --scan paths, one per allowlist directory, so dev/, ui-test/ and docs/ were never reached by this provisioning's invocation.
fixture.authored_shapes_follow: Dependency-Check 13.0.0's own report members, as verified against the raw artifact and the field names harness/lib/normalize/adapters/dependency_check.py reads: source, name, severity, unscored, cvssv2.score, cvssv3.baseScore, cvssv4.baseScore, cwes[], description, notes, references[], vulnerableSoftware[], packages[].id and the isVirtual/evidenceCollected pair a virtual dependency carries.
fixture.re_derivation_trigger: These rows are re-derived when the fixture changes, which is what the recorded sha256 above makes visible.

field_order_authority: harness/lib/normalize/emit.py, the FIELDS constant. Every row below carries all twelve keys in that order, present-with-null rather than omitted.
absence_convention: Absence is JSON null here and in findings.json, and an empty field in findings.csv. tool, scanner_class, rule_id, message, severity_norm, path and in_scope are never absent.

allowlist.note: in_scope is decided by that file alone. The globs are not copied here: the allowlist is the single authority and stays byte-exact. The glob each in-scope row matched is recorded per row under row_derivations, and each out-of-scope row records that it matched none.

resolution_context.root_dependence: Unlike the SARIF fixtures, every filePath in this artifact is filesystem-absolute and carries the root as a literal prefix, so these rows are stated for the root the fixture's own paths are under -- /opt/spark-src, the value harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json records as spark_src. The rows hold for any root the reported paths sit beneath; they are not root-independent in the way an already-root-relative uri is. The root is spelled out here and under path_base_value because the rows are stated against it; no row's path field is absolute, and none retains that prefix.
resolution_context.path_base_source: harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json, the dependency-check entry's path_base -- read as input, never assumed
resolution_context.path_base_evidence: The runner builds one absolute --scan argument per allowlist directory (18 in a single invocation, invocations_per_run 1), so dependencies[].filePath is filesystem-absolute under the scan root and the resolution is a straight relativization.
resolution_context.working_directory: /opt/spark-src -- equal to the scan root, and deliberately NOT the path base: the tool reports absolute paths because it was handed absolute --scan arguments, not because of where the process ran.
resolution_context.paths_exist_on_disk: All eight resolved paths name a file present in the pinned tree at 59b8a4489c878fa3a9aa6b7fbae760f2fc80eb9d, verified by inspection of the tree. That is a separate question from the path kind, and it is why non_filesystem_paths is 0 here.
resolution_context.start_line: null on every row, and deliberately so rather than by omission. Dependency-Check reports at dependency granularity -- a vulnerable component, not a line of code -- and this artifact carries no line information in any member, at any depth. Synthesising one would be inference. It is also why no reject-dependency-check-non-integer-start-line fixture exists: there is no start_line in this shape to be non-integer.
resolution_context.package_coordinate: Present on all eight rows. For this shape an unformable coordinate is a rejection rather than a null field, so a row reaching the dataset always carries one.
resolution_context.count_unit: dependencies[].vulnerabilities[] -- one vulnerability is one record

counts.raw_count_unit: one element of dependencies[].vulnerabilities[] -- the unit normalize.reconcile.count_records walks independently of row construction, summing len(vulnerabilities) over dependencies[]
counts.raw_count_derivation: sum(len(d.vulnerabilities)) over the eight dependencies = 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 2 + 1 + 0. The eighth dependency, core/src/main/resources/org/apache/spark/ui/static/package.json, carries no vulnerabilities key at all: it contributes no record, is not a rejection, and is counted under dependencies_without_vulnerabilities_array.
counts.independent_count_authority: harness/lib/normalize/reconcile.py, _count_dependency_check, reached through count_records('dependency-check', doc). It builds no row, which is the whole point of it: a count taken from the traversal that builds the rows satisfies the identity while testing nothing.

counters_authority: harness/lib/normalize/adapters/dependency_check.py, COUNTER_KEYS as returned by new_counters(): thirty-three keys in that order -- twenty-four authored, plus one path_kind_* per normalize.paths.PATH_KINDS member and one severity_basis_* per normalize.severity.BASIS_VALUES member.
counters_note: The four counters AAP 0.5.4 has reported per tool: multi_location_records 0 -- no dependency in this fixture carries a relatedDependencies array, which is the only multi-location shape this report has; multi_valued_cwe_records 1 -- row 2 alone, whose cwes array holds two distinct identifiers; multi_valued_cve_records 0 -- no record's name yields more than one CVE identifier; non_filesystem_paths 0 -- every path names a file inside the scanned tree, so neither the archive-member nor the outside-root kind occurs.
counters_arithmetic: dependencies 8 == the eight elements of dependencies[]
dependencies_skipped_non_mapping 0 + dependencies_without_vulnerabilities_array 1 == the one dependency contributing no record
rows_in_scope 4 + rows_out_of_scope 4 == rows 8 -- one measurement split, not a second count of the same thing
start_line_absent 8 == rows 8, by the policy stated in resolution_context.start_line
severity_basis_label 5 + severity_basis_cvss_score 3 == rows 8, and the other three bases are 0
path_kind_tree_file 8 == rows 8, and the other three kinds are 0

package_coordinate_precedence.authority: AAP 0.5.4's one candidate precedence for every dependency-oriented shape, implemented by harness/lib/normalize/adapters/dependency_check.py's package_coordinate().

levels.name: record_package_url
levels.rule: a package URL on the record itself, under purl, packageUrl, packageURL or package_url
levels.note: Row 2 is the level that proves the precedence is ordered rather than opportunistic: its enclosing package object also carries a package URL, 'pkg:javascript/datatables@1.13.11', and the record's own 'pkg:npm/datatables.net@1.13.11' is taken because level 1 stops first. An implementation that scanned packages[] before the record would emit the other value and every other row would still look right.

levels.name: package_object_package_url
levels.rule: else a package URL on the enclosing package object -- for this shape the enclosing dependency's packages[] entries, pooled across every entry before the tiebreak is applied
levels.note: The level that carries this artifact. Row 1 is the tiebreak case: two entries, two package URLs, and the lexicographically smallest wins.

levels.name: record_ecosystem_name_version
levels.rule: else <ecosystem>:<name>@<version> from the record's own fields, ecosystem lower-cased
levels.note: Reached by no row, and not because the fixture avoids it. A Dependency-Check vulnerability's name is the advisory identifier, so the adapter refuses a name equal to the record's own rule_id or CVE-shaped -- and every record here is one or the other. Row 3 is the row that reaches level 3 and is refused there, which is why its coordinate comes from level 4. Without that guard row 3 would form 'javascript:sonatype-2021-0163@...'-shaped nonsense and the unformable-coordinate rejection this shape genuinely produces would never fire.

levels.name: package_object_ecosystem_name_version
levels.rule: else the same triple from the enclosing package's fields
levels.note: Row 3 reaches level 4 for two stated reasons: its package object's id is a CPE, 'cpe:2.3:a:d3-flame-graph:d3-flame-graph:4.1.3:*:*:*:*:*:*:*', which is not a package URL and is never coerced into one, so level 2 offers nothing; and level 3 is refused as described above. The triple is formed from that same package object's ecosystem, name and version, with the ecosystem lower-cased from 'JavaScript' to 'javascript'.

package_coordinate_precedence.tiebreak: Where several candidates sit at one level the lexicographically smallest wins, over the pooled candidates of the whole level rather than within one package object -- taking the first entry's value instead would make the coordinate depend on producer order.

tiebreak_exercised_by.why: 'pkg:javascript/...' sorts before 'pkg:npm/...' because 'j' precedes 'n'. Producer order puts the npm entry first and marks it confidence LOW while the javascript entry is HIGH, so neither the array order nor the confidence field decides this: the stated lexicographic rule does, and it is the only one of the three that is reproducible.

package_coordinate_precedence.ecosystem_case: Lower-cased on the one row that forms a triple (row 3). The name and version are carried exactly as observed, since a package name is case-sensitive in several ecosystems and folding it would name a different package.
package_coordinate_precedence.absence: Where no candidate can be formed at any level the field is not emitted null: for this dependency-oriented shape the record is rejected under unformable_package_coordinate. That case belongs to oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/reject-dependency-check-no-package-coordinate.json and not here, which is why package_coordinate_unformable is 0 above. It is the realistic case rather than a contrived one: the raw artifact's 32 dependencies resolved zero package coordinates, all of them vendored web assets with no manifest behind them -- core/src/main/resources/org/apache/spark/ui/static/package.json, this fixture's eighth dependency, being 5 lines and 80 bytes with no dependencies block.

severity_policy.authority: harness/lib/normalize/severity.py -- the case-insensitive label map, the CVSS v3.1 section 5 band table, and resolve()'s ordered precedence. Nothing is mapped or banded in the adapter.
severity_policy.label_over_score: A native label in the mapped vocabulary governs whatever the scores say; a score is consulted only where no mapped label exists. Either way the entry used is recorded -- the label, or the score with its source and version.
severity_policy.bands: 9.0-10.0 Critical, 7.0-8.9 High, 4.0-6.9 Medium, 0.1-3.9 Low, 0.0 Info. The boundaries and the first four labels are the CVSS v3.1 section 5 standard's; the standard's None band is emitted under this dataset's own label Info, which is a mapping this dataset defines and not a CVSS label. Banding is by ordered numeric comparison, never lexical.
severity_policy.severity_native_rendering: A label reaches severity_native as the literal the tool wrote, stripped of surrounding whitespace and neither case-folded nor coerced -- which is why row 1 carries lower-case 'moderate'. A numeric severity reaches it as a one-decimal rendering of the full-precision value.

label_versus_score_disagreements.label: LOW
label_versus_score_disagreements.note: The reference disagreement, and a wide one: three CVSS blocks spanning Critical, Medium and Low sit on one record beside a LOW label. An implementation reading cvssv3 -- the usual choice -- emits Critical. Recorded precisely: had no mapped label existed, severity.py's own selection order (highest version first) would have taken cvssv4's 2.3 and banded Low, so the label-over-score rule does not change this row's band. What it changes is which entry is recorded as having governed it, and that is the checkable difference.

several_cvss_structures_on_one_record.selected: none -- the mapped label governed, so no score entry was consulted

cvssv3 -- the record carries no severity member at all, so the score candidates were consulted, and cvssv3 was selected over cvssv2 by the documented order: highest CVSS version first, version '3.1' above version '2.0'. Its baseScore 7.5 bands High. The recorded entry names both a source and a version, which is the one row incrementing severity_selected_score_with_source_and_version.
several_cvss_structures_on_one_record.source_composition: The block carries no source of its own, so the adapter composes the record's own source with the block key as 'NVD:cvssv3'. Neither half is invented: a block named cvssv3 is a version-3 entry, and the record's source is the provenance of the scores under it.

several_cvss_structures_on_one_record.selected: none -- the mapped label HIGH governed, and it agrees with cvssv3's 7.5
none -- the mapped label MEDIUM governed, and it agrees with cvssv3's 6.5

float_representation_artifacts.origin: An OSS Index-sourced record carries no label and Dependency-Check renders the provider's float CVSS score into the severity field, so the float32-to-float64 representation tail reaches the artifact verbatim. Both values are in the fixture exactly as written here.
float_representation_artifacts.banding: Numeric, on the full-precision value rather than on the rendered text. Each of the two values recorded above under measured_values bands exactly as its one-decimal rendering does -- the first Low, the second Medium -- because the comparison is an ordered numeric one and never a lexical one. Rounding to one decimal place cannot cross a band boundary at either value, and the band is never taken from the rendered text.
float_representation_artifacts.no_spurious_precision: severity_native carries the one-decimal rendering, so no artifact tail reaches a text field. The full-precision value appears in this file only as a JSON number under a selected_entry score -- which is where severity.py keeps it -- and inside no prose or text field anywhere.
float_representation_artifacts.path_taken: These two rows reach the numeric branch because the severity member is a JSON number rather than a mapped label and neither record carries a CVSS block: the value is banded as a score in its own right, and the recorded entry names source 'label' with a null version, which is why neither row increments severity_selected_score_with_source_and_version.

case_insensitivity.note: Absorbed by the case-insensitive map, whose keys are upper-case and whose lookup upper-cases the observed literal. The literal is preserved as written rather than folded, because severity-map.md reports observed literals with per-literal row counts and upper-casing it here would misreport a literal the tool never wrote.

severity_policy.never_absent: severity_norm is absent on no row. severity_native is absent on no row either -- every record here carries either a severity member or a bandable score -- so the no_vocabulary basis, which is the only path setting severity_native null, is 0.
severity_policy.unmapped_literals: None. Every literal in this fixture is either a mapped label or a bandable number in 0.0-10.0, so severity_basis_unmapped_literal is 0.

corroboration.note: The opengrep expectation cross-checks its rows against oss-scan-results/findings.json after the fact. That is not available here and its absence is stated rather than papered over: dependency-check reported zero findings over the twelve authoritative roots, so it contributes no row to the committed dataset and there is nothing in it to compare these eight rows against. They rest on the fixture and the authored contracts alone, which is what AAP 0.6.2 asks of a hand-verified expected file in any case. The scope fact behind the zero is reported in oss-scan-results/tool-status.md, not here.

rows.message: Bootstrap contains a cross-site scripting weakness in the carousel component: the data-slide and data-slide-to attributes are written into the document without neutralizing markup, so a page that renders attacker-influenced attribute values can execute script in the browsing context of the page.

The cookie accessor evaluates a stored cookie value as structured data before returning it, so a cookie written by another document on the same registrable domain can influence the object the caller receives.

A prototype pollution weakness in the table initialization path: a configuration object read from untrusted input is merged into a shared prototype, so a crafted key can add or replace properties visible to every later object.
The flame graph builder copies keys from a supplied node object onto an internal accumulator without excluding prototype-reaching names, so a crafted node label can reach the object prototype.
The glob prefix parser backtracks on a pattern containing many nested braces, so a long crafted pattern costs time superlinear in its length.

Passing HTML containing option elements from untrusted sources to a DOM manipulation method can execute the script those elements carry, even after the markup has been passed through the library's own sanitizing helper.
HTML from an untrusted source, even after being passed through the library's sanitizing helper, may execute script when it is inserted into the document.
Parsing an XML document containing many digits in a numeric character reference takes time superlinear in the length of the reference, so a small document can occupy the parser for a long time.
